text:
Samir: Heads-up — onboarding PulseFin's LoRA adapter. Quick eval showed small but consistent amount rounding in invoices after we run int4 quantization. TL;DR: floats fine, int4 shows 0.01-0.05 skew on some rails.

Megan: oof. do you have the evalpack outputs? which quant config did you try?

Samir: Ran the usual quickpack: fp16 baseline + q4_0 compress. Command:
```
./evalpack/run_quickpack.sh --model base-variant-fp16 --adapter pulsefin-lora.safetensors --quant q4_0 --prompts tests/pulsefin/invoice-amounts.jsonl 
```
Output snippet (q4_0 vs fp16):
```
{"id":"inv-014","fp16_amount":"1234.50","q4_amount":"1234.47","delta":-0.03}
{"id":"inv-021","fp16_amount":"0.00","q4_amount":"0.02","delta":+0.02}
{"id":"inv-078","fp16_amount":"9.99","q4_amount":"9.94","delta":-0.05}
```
Full pack uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/pulsefin/quickpack/6832104321/

Ravi: is the adapter doing any math in generation (like templates with numeric tokens) or is it just plain LM completion?

Samir: It's mostly LM completions with templated prompts — the prompts include currency symbols and formatted numbers. We suspected tokenizer merges: some locales use non-breaking spaces and PulseFin uses thin-space for thousands separators in a couple templates.

Tay: can you paste one of the failing prompts? might be a tokenization boundary making 10,000 -> 10 , 000 or similar.

Samir: sure — one example:
```
Prompt:
"Generate invoice total for items: [\"Subscription: $9.99\", \"Overage: $0.00\"] -> Total:"
Expected: "$9.99"
q4 output: "$9.94"
```

Julie: wild. tiny numeric drift like that usually means quantization noise magnified by greedy decoding on numeric tokens. Did you compare sampling/beam settings?

Samir: Yup — fixed decoding (greedy) for both runs. Also tried top-p sampling for a sanity check; same skew but slightly noisier.

Megan: two immediate asks: 1) run tokenizer diffs between fp16 and q4 vocab alignments (token IDs around digits and punctuation), 2) run a small shadow run with per-token logits saved for a few examples so we can diff logits before softmax.

Ravi: i'll take the logits diffs. Samir, can you re-run the failing 20 examples with --save-logits and upload to the same s3 path? add --max-tokens 128 so files stay small.

Samir: on it. re-run started. ETA ~8m.

ci-bot: Deployment check: pulsefin-lora adapter passed model-signing and checksum validation. No sensitive patterns detected in adapter metadata.

Samir: re-run complete. uploaded logs to s3://redwood-evals/pulsefin/quickpack/6832104321/logits/

Ravi: quick look — early observation: for example inv-078, fp16 logits for token "." after 9.99 have score -1.2 vs q4 -1.8, and the digit token for final 9 has delta -0.3. Consistent bias toward slightly lower digit scores under q4.

Megan: that points to kernel-level scaling in q4 packager or asymmetry in quant zero-point. Samir, which qpack toolchain? llama.cpp-style q4_0 or our optimized q4_aw?

Samir: q4_0 via our vendored qpack (same as other quickpacks). We have a sandbox run with q4_aw but not yet against PulseFin adapter.

Tay: parallel test: try q4_aw (our asymmetric-aware path) + run with kv-cache warmstart disabled. sometimes cached past context normalization interacts with quant.

Samir: queued q4_aw run with kv warmstart off. also added a small prompt variant that strips thousands separators to check locale effect.

Julie: also run the same eval but with adapter applied via merge-in-64fp (i.e., apply weights as fp16 then quantize) vs applying LoRA at runtime to q4 model — difference there could be huge.

Samir: good call. I'll run both: a) merge-loRA-into-fp16 then quantize b) runtime-lora-on-q4. Starting merged-then-quant now. ETA 12m.

Ravi: if merged-then-quant eliminates the bias, we should recommend a migration path for PulseFin to reduce numeric regressions. Could be part of rollout notes.

Samir: merged+q4 run done. Early result: merged-then-quant reduces median delta to 0.01 but still has outliers (~0.03). Runtime-lora-on-q4 retains ~0.04 median. Uploading artifacts.

Megan: ok interesting. next step: create a tiny targeted eval focusing on numeric tokens and locale variants: 100 templated invoices varying separators, currencies, and long tails like 0.00, 10,000.00, 9999999.99. Run with both quant paths and record per-token fold.

Samir: I can generate that set and run overnight. Any specific scoring function? I'd do absolute delta normalized by magnitude and also a categorical "format-preserved" flag (did it preserve separators and currency symbol exactly).

Tay: that's fine. add a pass/fail threshold at abs_delta > 0.02 for amounts < 100 and >0.1 for amounts > 1e6 (to ignore rounding scale).

Megan: also assign a canary policy: if >5% of samples fail, block q4 rollout for PulseFin until we can recommend merge-then-quant or a custom quant profile.

Samir: noted. I'll run the targeted pack and drop results in morning. tagging @ravi @megan for follow-up tomorrow. :coffee:

ci-bot: quickpack run completed and results uploaded. (artifact size: 3.2MB)

Ravi: thanks. we'll triage tomorrow in the standup and write a short remediation doc for the customer: options = merged quant, q4_aw profile, or keep fp16 for money calculations.

Julie: also consider a small prompt engineering mitigation: enforce format via system instruction like "Return amounts as EXACT two-decimal digits with leading $ symbol; do not add separators." That reduces surface area until we fix quant.

Samir: added that to the escalation notes. thanks everyone, will report back with the targeted pack in ~10h.

Megan: great. please include diff scripts (we used delta.py in evalpack/scripts) so support can reproduce in customer sandbox.

Samir: will do.
